source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"CK-MB primarily evaluates renal filtration and has no recognized relationship to myocardium","B":"CK-MB is more cardiac-specific than troponin and should replace serial troponin testing","C":"CK-MB can indicate myocardial injury, but cardiac troponin is the preferred biomarker today","D":"CK-MB alone proves acute myocardial infarction regardless of symptoms, ECG, or serial testing"}}
source_row.rationale: CK-MB may rise with myocardial injury, but current chest-pain guidance identifies cardiac troponin, especially high-sensitivity troponin, as the preferred biomarker for myocardial injury. Biomarkers require clinical and ECG correlation.
source_row.source_detail: Biomarkers section: serial cardiac troponin I/T is preferred for myocardial injury; high-sensitivity troponin preferred; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: ACC/AHA — 2021 Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain
source_row.stem: A client with chest pain has an elevated CK-MB value. Which statement best reflects current cardiac biomarker practice?
